dimensions.detail: The code and instructions match the stated purpose: collect OpenClaw metadata, package local skills or code projects, upload them to Trent, and request security analysis.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Phase 2 clearly says to preview discovered skills and wait for confirmation before uploading; Phase 1 immediately sends redacted configuration metadata to Trent as part of the requested audit workflow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No installer, dependency fetch, or auto-start behavior was found; the skill uses bundled Python modules and requires a TRENT_API_KEY environment variable.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Reading ~/.openclaw and ~/.openclaw/workspace is proportionate for an OpenClaw security audit, but it can include proprietary skill source code and configuration metadata.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill writes temporary chat output and creates .skill ZIP packages in the workspace before upload; no background persistence, privilege escalation, destructive file changes, or credential-store access was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The file, environment, shell, and network capabilities are real, but they are used for the documented Trent audit flow; the artifact declares the required API key and describes the data collection/upload steps.
[TP4] expected: Workspace scanning, packaging, redaction, and upload are sensitive but purpose-aligned and disclosed in the Phase 2 instructions, including a required user confirmation before upload.
[SQP-2] expected: The privacy disclosure could be more prominent near the top, especially for Phase 1 metadata transmission, but the workflow does state that metadata is sent to Trent and that skill source packages are previewed before upload.
llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending redacted OpenClaw configuration metadata and, after confirmation, packaged skill/source code to Trent. Review the Phase 2 preview carefully, keep secrets in environment variables rather than source files, and delete generated .skill archives if you do not want local packaged copies to remain.
llm.summary: This skill is a cloud-backed security audit helper that reads OpenClaw configuration and workspace skill code, redacts common secrets, and sends selected data to Trent with user confirmation before skill uploads.
